texts.facts: Petitioner has filed this writ petition aggrieved with the action of sealing of her shops No. G-1, 2, 3, 4 & 5 at Cross Road Business Park, Vyapar Vihar, Bilaspur by respondent No.5 without issuing any notice or passing any order against petitioner. 2. Learned counsel for petitioner submits that petitioner has established two units namely Daily Dose Bakery and Xero Degree Cafe in shop No. G-1, 2, 3, 4 & 5 of ground floor of Cross Road Business Park situated in front of Mahima Complex, Vyapar Vihar Bilaspur after obtaining valid Gumasta license, food license etc. The said shops are owned by respondent No.6, who executed the lease deed in favour of proprietor of petitioner's firm on 31st of October, 2022. At the time of execution of lease deed, respondent No.6 informed petitioner that shopping complex was constructed after fulfilling all the formalities, obtaining due permission from the competent authority in accordance with law. After taking aforementioned shops on lease, petitioner invested huge amount for starting aforementioned business. Respondent No.5 on 28.02.2023 suddenly came to the shop of petitioner and sealed the shop let out to petitioner on which petitioner is running her business. The action on the part of respondent no.2 and 5 is highly arbitrary and in violation of Article 19 (1) (g) of the Constitution of India. Referring to the reply submitted by respondents No.2 and 5 he contended that in reply, there is pleading that shops occupied by petitioner was sealed for the purpose of demolition of fourth floor which was illegally constructed which also is after thought. According to her information, even the respondent No.6 was not served with any notice, even if any part of building is unauthorizedly constructed without prior approval and permission of the competent authority. Hence, entire action of on the part of respondents is not sustainable. Therefore, respondents be directed to unseal the shops of petitioner immediately. Respondent No.6 had applied for building permission, which was allowed and he was permitted to construct complex in terms of the proposal submitted and accepted by answering respondents. Respondent No.6 completed the construction of 3rd floor of the aforementioned A And B Foods vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 4 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46616612/ 2 complex along with basement according to proposal. He has also been issued completion certificate for the same. Respondent No.6 by deceiving the answering respondents obtained completion certificate, however, he continued with the construction of one more floor i.e. fourth floor. After getting knowledge of illegal construction of fourth floor by respondent No.6, notice was issued to him, however, he did not appear nor replied the said notice. Some complaints were also received against petitioner, hence, respondent No.4 also joined with respondent No.5 along with State machinery and visited the complex of respondent No.6 on 28.02.2023 to take actions against illegal construction and the violation of food norms by petitioner. Respondent No.4 proceeded to move against petitioner and the rest of the team proceeded to move against other operational shops. He also argued that respondent No.4 took few samples and thereafter answering respondents moved ahead with their procedure.
texts.arguments: 3. It is further contention of learned counsel for petitioner that before taking adverse action of sealing the entire running shops of petitioner no notice of any kind has been served upon petitioner and even she was not informed about the same by respondent No.5 as to for what reasons, the shops have been sealed. He contended that petitioner thereafter also approached the authorities i.e. the office of respondents No.2 and 5 to know about the reason and the provision under which her shops were sealed, however, they have not given any information nor served with any order till the date of filing of writ petition. 4. Learned counsel for respondents No.6 submits that respondent No.2 and 5 have not issued any notice to respondent No.6 at any point of time before taking action of sealing of shops leased out to petitioner. It is contention of learned counsel for respondent No.6 that respondent No.6 has already submitted an application for regularization of construction along with map which is pending consideration and which is also acknowledged by respondents No.2 and 5 in their return. 5. Learned counsel for respondents No.2 and 5 submits that there is no dispute with respect to running of business by petitioner on the shop No. G-1, 2, 3, 4 & 5 at Cross Road Business Park, Vyapar Vihar, Bilaspur after obtaining those shops on lease from respondent No.6. There is no direct conflicting issue with petitioner but with respondent no.6 on account of illegal construction of fourth floor. It is further contention of learned counsel for respondent No.2 & 5 that samples collected by respondent No.4 was found to be sub-standard. Petitioner is trying to bypass and move around the notice of eviction served upon respondent No.6 for which petitioner is having the alternate remedy. The claim of petitioner that no action has been taken against respondent No.6 but only against petitioner is not correct as the action is being taken only against respondent No.6 and not against any other persons. 6. In reply, learned counsel for petitioner submits that it is the complex of three floor in which more than 40 shops are constructed out of which shops of petitioner is only sealed. 8. The main contention of learned counsel for petitioner is that shop of petitioner is sealed without any authority of law and that too by adopting pick and choose method only.
